result.topic_en: Euler opens Chapter XIV on quadratic residues modulo composite numbers, treating the residues of squares coprime to the divisor 2(2p+1), twice a prime, and comparing them with the residues modulo the prime 2p+1 in a table of examples.
result.transcription:
Tractatus de numerorum doctrina Cap. 14. 65
Caput XIV.
De residuis, ex divisione quadratorum per numeros compositos ortis.
502. Sint 1, $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$, $\delta$, etc. residua, quae ex divisione quadratorum per numerum primum $2p+1$ oriuntur, quorum numerus est $=p$; ac videamus primo, quaenam residua oriantur, si divisio fiat per duplum $2(2p+1)$, atque hic quidem excludamus quadrata paria; tantum enim ea quadrata, quae ad divisorem sunt prima, consideremus.
503. Multitudo autem quadratorum, quorum radices sunt divisore minores, est $=2p$, et quoniam quadrata $aa$ et $(4p+2-a)^2$ idem relinquunt residuum, multitudo residuorum diversorum major esse nequit quam $p$; erit ergo vel $=p$, vel minor quam $p$.
504. Minor scilicet esset, si darentur duo quadrata $aa$ et $bb$, ut non esset $b=4p+2-a$, quae idem relinquerent residuum. Foret autem tum $bb-aa=(b-a)(b+a)$ divisibile per $2(2p+1)$, et alter factor per 2, alter per $2p+1$ divisibilis esse deberet. At uno existente pari, alter quoque erit par, ideoque per totum divisorem divisibilis, unde foret $b=2(2p+1)-a$.
505. Multitudo ergo residuorum diversorum, quae quidem ex quadratis ad divisorem primis oriuntur, erit $=p$, totidem numero, quot ex divisore primo $2p+1$ nascuntur. Ac si residua, ex divisore $2(2p+1)$ orta, sint 1, $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$, etc., eorum numerus est $=p$, et ibidem occurrent producta ex binis.
506. Dantur autem $2p$ numeri ad hunc divisorem primi eoque minores, unde cum eorum tantum semissis residua constituat, alter semissis dabit ordinem non-residuorum, quae si sint $\mathfrak{A}$, $\mathfrak{B}$, $\mathfrak{C}$, $\mathfrak{D}$, etc., eorum numerus erit $=p$, et producta ex horum binis iterum fient residua.
507. Contemplemur quaedam exempla, in iisque tam residua, quae ex divisore primo $2p+1$, quam ex ejus duplo $2(2p+1)$ nascuntur, simulque apponamus non-residua ad divisorem prima:
divisor 3 | 6 | 5 | 10 | 7 | 14
residua 1 | 1 | 1, 4 | 1, 9 | 1, 2, 4 | 1, 9, 11
non-residua 2 | 5 | 2, 3 | 3, 7 | 3, 5, 6 | 3, 5, 13
divisor 11 | 22
residua 1, 3, 9, 5, 4 | 1, 9, 3, 5, 15
non-residua 2, 6, 7, 8, 10 | 7, 13, 17, 19, 21
divisor 13 | 26
residua 1, 3, 4, 9, 10, 12 | 1, 3, 9, 17, 23, 25
non-residua 2, 5, 6, 7, 8, 11 | 5, 7, 11, 15, 19, 21
divisor 17 | 34
residua 1, 2, 4, 8, 9, 13, 15, 16 | 1, 9, 13, 15, 19, 21, 25, 33
non-residua 3, 5, 6, 7, 10, 11, 12, 14 | 3, 5, 7, 11, 23, 27, 29, 31
508. Repraesentemus rem in genere:
divisor $2p+1$ | $2(2p+1)$
residua 1, $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$, $\delta$, etc. | 1, $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$, etc.
non-residua $\mathfrak{a}$, $\mathfrak{b}$, $\mathfrak{c}$, $\mathfrak{d}$, $\mathfrak{e}$, etc. | $\mathfrak{A}$, $\mathfrak{B}$, $\mathfrak{C}$, $\mathfrak{D}$, $\mathfrak{E}$, etc.
L. Euleri Op. posthuma. T. I. 9

methods.what: Squares of a and of 2(2p+1)-a leave the same residue mod 2(2p+1), so there are at most p distinct residues
methods.quote: quoniam quadrata $aa$ et $(4p+2-a)^2$ idem relinquunt residuum, multitudo residuorum diversorum major esse nequit quam $p$

methods.what: Proof that the number of distinct residues coprime to 2(2p+1) is exactly p, by factoring bb-aa and using parity
methods.quote: Foret autem tum $bb-aa=(b-a)(b+a)$ divisibile per $2(2p+1)$, et alter factor per 2, alter per $2p+1$ divisibilis esse deberet. At uno existente pari, alter quoque erit par, ideoque per totum divisorem divisibilis, unde foret $b=2(2p+1)-a$.

methods.what: Mod 2(2p+1) there are exactly p residues among the coprime numbers, the same count as mod the prime 2p+1
methods.quote: Multitudo ergo residuorum diversorum, quae quidem ex quadratis ad divisorem primis oriuntur, erit $=p$, totidem numero, quot ex divisore primo $2p+1$ nascuntur.

methods.what: Products of two residues are residues
methods.quote: et ibidem occurrent producta ex binis

methods.what: There are 2p numbers coprime to the divisor; half are residues and half (p) are non-residues; the product of two non-residues is a residue
methods.quote: Dantur autem $2p$ numeri ad hunc divisorem primi eoque minores, unde cum eorum tantum semissis residua constituat, alter semissis dabit ordinem non-residuorum, quae si sint $\mathfrak{A}$, $\mathfrak{B}$, $\mathfrak{C}$, $\mathfrak{D}$, etc., eorum numerus erit $=p$, et producta ex horum binis iterum fient residua.

methods.what: Table of quadratic residues and non-residues modulo 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17 and their doubles 6, 10, 14, 22, 26, 34
methods.quote: Contemplemur quaedam exempla, in iisque tam residua, quae ex divisore primo $2p+1$, quam ex ejus duplo $2(2p+1)$ nascuntur, simulque apponamus non-residua ad divisorem prima

items.quote: ac videamus primo, quaenam residua oriantur, si divisio fiat per duplum $2(2p+1)$, atque hic quidem excludamus quadrata paria; tantum enim ea quadrata, quae ad divisorem sunt prima, consideremus.
items.english: and let us first see which residues arise if the division is made by the double 2(2p+1); here we exclude even squares, for we consider only those squares which are prime to the divisor.

items.quote: et ibidem occurrent producta ex binis
items.english: and among them will occur the products of any two of them

items.quote: et producta ex horum binis iterum fient residua
items.english: and the products of any two of these will again be residues
